verdicts.quote: opens the bot from inside Salesforce, and sees a place to enter a prompt
verdicts.missing: Which Salesforce surface hosts the bot (record page component, utility bar, Experience Cloud, Flow) and what context that surface passes in.

verdicts.quote: A bot request does not retrieve Salesforce business records.
The record, its fields, and other business data are absent from the outbound request unless the user supplied them in the prompt.
The org administrator can grant bot access to a Salesforce user.
One Salesforce user cannot read another user's prompts or replies through the bot.
verdicts.missing: Whether and how an administrator can access users' prompts and replies.

verdicts.quote: The bot keeps the xAI credential out of user-visible output.
verdicts.missing: Where the credential is stored (Named/External Credential or protected setting) and that it never appears in code, metadata or logs.

verdicts.quote: The bot resolves a request as timed out if no completed outcome is available within 120 seconds of submission.
verdicts.missing: The Salesforce governor limits that bind the design (callout timeout ceiling, callouts per transaction, heap, CPU time) with their numbers.

verdicts.quote: Delay the Grok reply and observe a pending state before the result is available.
verdicts.missing: The mechanism by which the interface learns the reply arrived (platform event, polled status, LMS, etc.).

verdicts.quote: A failed submission is not automatically resubmitted by the bot.
verdicts.missing: Idempotency so a retried or re-enqueued async job cannot post the same reply twice.

verdicts.quote: Submit a prompt while Salesforce or xAI denies processing with a reported capacity or spending restriction
verdicts.missing: The queue-depth or concurrent-job limits and what happens to a request that cannot be enqueued.

verdicts.quote: The bot tells the user when the service rejects the prompt itself. ... return an HTTP 5xx error ... The user sees a failure ... The bot reports a timeout by that boundary.
When xAI returns HTTP 429, the user sees that a usage limit was reached and can try again later. ... no further inference attempt is made for it until the user submits again.
Return partial text accompanied by a provider truncation indication. The bot identifies the reply as incomplete. ... The bot reports a timeout by that boundary.
The bot does not provide saved conversations.
verdicts.missing: Whether exchanges are stored at all and, if so, the record shape (role, text, status, timestamps, model identifier, usage counts).

verdicts.quote: The bot does not automatically transfer Salesforce business data to xAI. ... find that prompt text will be sent to xAI before sending a prompt.
Each request uses the current prompt independently of other prompts. ... the bot identifies the input as too large for the model. ... The bot does not silently shorten the prompt
asks Grok a question for the first time ... rejects a prompt containing zero non-whitespace characters ... a prompt of exactly 4,000 Unicode code points passes length validation
The administrator can select an available Grok text model. ... The administrator learns whether a failed request needs setup attention
verdicts.missing: A switch to turn the bot off for everyone and a way for the administrator to view failed requests.

verdicts.quote: Introducing the bot does not change a production Salesforce org.
verdicts.missing: How configuration and credentials differ per environment and the deployment path (scratch org/sandbox, metadata deployment, production code-coverage requirement).

verdicts.missing: An initial empty state and any standard for deliberate visual design beyond functional indications.

verdicts.quote: Bot deployment leaves pre-existing Salesforce business data intact. ... Their effective access is unchanged. ... Its configured triggers and outcomes stay the same.
